subject: Livechat degraded throughput — mitigation plan & telemetry package
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Livechat degraded throughput — immediate mitigation steps

Hi Aisha,

Wanted to flag that we observed a sustained increase in end-to-end latency for Greenline Health's streaming/chat endpoints starting ~08:45 PDT. Users intermittently see pauses of 3–8s between streamed chunks and in some cases the stream stalls entirely before reconnecting. We're treating this as a high-priority incident.

Immediate actions we've taken (already applied):
- Throttled non-critical background streams for your account to free capacity.
- Enabled a short-lived model-variant fallback (lower-batched quantized variant) for new sessions to reduce token generation latency.
- Pushed a client-side recommendation (see checklist) to temporarily switch long-poll polling for critical flows while we stabilize streaming.

Requested action from Greenline (quick wins):
- If possible, reduce max_concurrent_streams per user to 2 for the next 2 hours.
- For urgent user journeys (login/checkout), switch to our HTTP poll path (non-streaming) — this is a config toggle and we can flip it remotely if you approve.

What we're doing next:
- SRE is collecting per-shard KV-cache hit/miss metrics and tracing any backpressure in the encoder pipeline.
- We'll share a telemetry tarball and a short runbook for your engineers in the next 60–90 minutes.
- We will schedule a customer-visible update at +1h and a more complete post-incident summary within 24 hours.

Attachments: telemetry extract (CSV), temporary runbook (PDF), customer action checklist (MD).

I know this is disruptive — we're focused on restoring the streaming experience quickly and will keep you updated every hour.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0127

Subject: RE: Livechat degraded throughput — immediate mitigation steps

Hi Aisha —

We have SRE on a hotfix path. Quick technical summary (high level):
- Root cause so far: a combination of an uneven KV-cache warming pattern on a recently deployed fractional routing change and a transient encoder-side queuing accumulation under peak token-burst load. In plain terms, some streaming shards saw a rapid sequence of long-context sessions which led to backpressure and slowed chunk emission.

Temporary mitigations we have applied (technical):
- Forced cache warm-up on affected shards and rebalanced routing for new sessions.
- Shortened internal chunk window to reduce per-chunk work and avoid queuing spikes.
- Rolled back the fractional routing change for sessions created in the last 4 hours.

What we recommend for Greenline right now (safe & reversible):
1) Flip critical flows to polling (you approved this) — minimal risk of message loss; we'll mark resumed streamed sessions in the logs to reconcile any partial replies.
2) Reduce client-side max_tokens_per_chunk to 128 for 2–3 hours (this reduces encoder latency spikes).
3) If you can, add a single-line diagnostic header to requests (X-RWF-Client: gl-platform-v2) so our downstream tooling can correlate traces without PII.

We're pushing telemetry and the runbook link into the ticket (INF-4231). I'll be on the bridge and will post another customer update at 10:15 PDT.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Post-incident summary: streaming latency event (timeline, root cause, next steps)

Hi Aisha and team,

Thanks again for your patience. Below is the post-incident summary for the streaming latency event that began 2028-07-25 08:45 PDT and materially impacted live chat for Greenline Health.

Summary and impact:
- Impact window: 2028-07-25 08:45 PDT -> 2028-07-25 12:30 PDT (material streaming latency/partial stalls).
- User-visible median chunk latency increase: 1.2s -> 3.8s. Peak stall fraction: ~4.5% of active sessions.

Root cause:
- A recent fractional routing adjustment caused uneven session placement across streaming shards. Several shards received disproportionate long-context sessions, which caused KV-cache cold hits and encoder queue accumulation. The combination produced backpressure that increased chunk emission latency — we refer to the cascade internally as a "stream splintering" event.

Corrective actions taken:
- Immediate roll-back of the fractional routing change and forced cache warm-up on all impacted shards.
- Short-term encoder chunk window reduction and a guarded model-variant fallback for new sessions.
- Exposed a configuration toggle for customers to fall back to polling without message loss.

Longer-term remediation (planned):
- Improved routing determinism and pre-warming for known long-context tenants (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Instrumentation to detect KV-cache skew and trigger proactive rebalancing (ETA: 3 weeks).
- Permanent change to chunk sizing heuristics to avoid queue amplification under token bursts (ETA: 4 weeks).

Customer action checklist (what we recommend you keep in place until we verify stability):
- Keep login/checkout flows on polling for 12–24 hours.
- Set max_tokens_per_chunk to 128 for high-concurrency sessions for the next 24 hours.
- Add diagnostic request header X-RWF-Client for improved correlation.

Compensation and follow-ups:
- One-time credit applied for the 6-hour affected window; Ben will email a credit summary and invoice adjustment.
- 30-minute technical review set for 2028-07-26 09:00 PDT (if you prefer alternate times let us know).
- Final verification update to confirm routing hardening will be posted to INF-4231.

Attached: detailed telemetry extract, runbook used during mitigation, and the customer action checklist.

If you'd like, we'll keep a dedicated SRE on the morning bridge tomorrow while you ramp back to streaming.

Sincerely,

Account Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
